skill.name: ask-graphql-mcp
skill.description: Use Ask GraphQL MCP to answer Web3 and on-chain questions against SubQuery, SubGraph, and other GraphQL endpoints.
skill.summary: Route Web3 GraphQL questions through Ask GraphQL MCP for endpoint-aware analysis and query help.
skill.author: SN-Hermes

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and system-reconnaissance alerts are Markdown false positives. The skill still routes data to an external MCP gateway and includes instructions that can expose API keys or private endpoint authorization headers. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to send API keys in chat.
remediation.suggestion: Use secure secret storage or environment variables, and instruct users to avoid pasting raw API keys into conversation text.

remediation.issue: Private endpoint authorization can be forwarded to a third-party gateway.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before forwarding authorization headers, require scoped temporary tokens, and document where headers are sent.

remediation.issue: External network calls are core to the skill behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Document that Ask MCP receives user tasks, endpoint URLs, and selected headers before any gateway request is made.

content.value_statement: Blockchain teams need fast answers from SubQuery and SubGraph endpoints. This skill routes natural-language questions through Ask GraphQL MCP for endpoint-aware analysis.
actual_capabilities: Routes Web3 and on-chain questions to graphql_agent through a session tool or HTTP JSON-RPC.
Uses the free Ask MCP gateway by default and paid mode after quota limits or user request.
Supports user-provided GraphQL endpoints with optional upstream authorization headers.
Provides setup templates for free and paid MCP configurations.
Offers prompt patterns for endpoint inspection, analytics, and query debugging.
Handles rate-limit responses with API key setup guidance.
limitations: Requires a reachable GraphQL endpoint before execution.
Sends endpoint details and user tasks to the external Ask MCP gateway.
Paid mode requires a user-provided Ask MCP API key and available provider quota.
Does not run direct GraphQL queries unless the user requests an MCP bypass.

use_cases.title: Analyze protocol activity
use_cases.description: Ask for on-chain metrics, active accounts, volume trends, or staking activity from a supported GraphQL endpoint.

use_cases.title: Debug endpoint queries
use_cases.description: Diagnose GraphQL errors, missing fields, schema mismatches, and pagination issues with MCP-assisted reasoning.

use_cases.title: Configure MCP access
use_cases.description: Create free or paid Ask MCP connection guidance for a user-provided SubQuery or SubGraph endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to an endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with a known public endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ask GraphQL MCP with this endpoint: <endpoint>. Confirm connectivity and summarize what data it indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect available data
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore a new SubQuery or SubGraph endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this endpoint with Ask GraphQL MCP and describe the main entities, useful metrics, and any schema assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a failing query
prompt_templates.scenario: Fix a query error without bypassing MCP.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ask GraphQL MCP to explain this query error and suggest a compatible query shape for the endpoint schema.

prompt_templates.title: Design dashboard metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis for product or analytics dashboards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ask GraphQL MCP to propose three dashboard metrics for this protocol and explain the endpoint fields needed for each metric.

output_examples.input: Analyze recent activity for this SubQuery endpoint.
output: States the endpoint assumptions and MCP connection status.
Summarizes active accounts, volume direction, and time window limits.
Lists follow-up checks for schema fields or pagination.

output_examples.input: My GraphQL query fails on a field name.
output: Explains the likely schema mismatch in plain language.
Suggests compatible field alternatives returned by MCP.
Recommends a small verification step before running a full analysis.

output_examples.input: Set up Ask MCP after the free quota is reached.
output: Identifies paid mode as the next path.
Describes the required gateway, endpoint header, and API key header.
Warns the user to keep secrets scoped and avoid sharing broad credentials.

best_practices: Use public endpoints or narrowly scoped endpoint tokens whenever possible.
Start in free mode and switch to paid mode only after quota limits or explicit user request.
Remove or redact secrets before sharing logs, errors, or configuration snippets.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad production credentials for endpoint authorization.
Do not use this skill for non-Web3 questions or general database work.
Do not bypass Ask MCP with direct GraphQL execution unless the user requests it.

faq.question: What endpoints does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is designed for GraphQL endpoints used by Web3 projects, including SubQuery and SubGraph endpoints.

faq.question: Does it need an endpoint URL?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use endpoint discovery first, but execution needs a reliable GraphQL endpoint.

faq.question: Does the skill call an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes requests through the Ask GraphQL MCP gateway.

faq.question: When is paid mode used?
faq.answer: Paid mode is used only after free-tier quota limits or when the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: Can it debug GraphQL errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask MCP to inspect schema issues, missing fields, and query shape problems.

faq.question: Should users share secrets?
faq.answer: Users should avoid broad secrets and use scoped, temporary credentials when private endpoint access is required.
